item.title: Leaky Chrome extensions with 37M installs caught divulging your browsing history

item.description: OpenAI has hired Peter Steinberger, creator of the viral OpenClaw AI assistant, to spearhead development of what CEO Sam Altman describes as “the next generation of personal agents.” The move comes weeks after OpenClaw, previously known as Clawdbot and then Moltbot, achieved explosive popularity despite security researchers warning of serious vulnerabilities in the open-source tool. item.title: The AI bubble will burst for firms that can’t get beyond demos and LLMs
item.description: The AI bubble isn’t just hype — it’s real and could create many corporate casualties if or when it bursts. The companies that will succeed will be the ones solving real-world problems and engaging clients, according to tech industry execs and analysts. item.title: Exploit available for new Chrome zero-day vulnerability, says Google
item.description: Threat actors now have the ability to exploit a new zero-day vulnerability in the Chrome browser, Google has advised IT administrators. item.title: Swedish AI browser Strawberry is now available to everyone
item.description: Stockholm-based Strawberry is launching its “self-driving” AI-powered browser in open beta after a year in closed testing. Strawberry is a browser with built-in AI agents that can surf, click, and perform real tasks on behalf of the user, even on login-protected sites. The idea is to make AI agents available to non-technical users such as salespeople, recruiters, and analysts, without them needing to be able to write advanced prompts or code. item.title: With physical AI, gunslingers and risk takers need not apply
item.description: Agentic AI came on like a storm over the past year or so, but blazed a trail littered with failed projects and cutting-edge high-tech junk that companies are still trying to sort out. So it’s perhaps no surprise that tech industry execs are urging enterprises to move cautiously with physical AI, where mistakes can have far-reaching business and societal consequences. “We need clear boundaries…, definitions, and rules,” said Tianlan Shao, CEO of Mech-Mind Robotics, which makes industrial robots.
